definition: Empirical constraints, not a computed Hamiltonian phase diagram.
method: Weighted Gaussian least squares in the supplied observable (1/T1 or rho), not logarithms. Independent quoted sigmas; no rescaling by reduced chi square. Parametric bootstrap, fixed supplied sigmas, seed 20261028.
empirical_fit_limitations: No covariance of normalization errors is supplied; fits are conditional on independent quoted errors.
NMR activation is not automatically a microscopic singlet-triplet gap.
Transport activation is not automatically the STS gap or half of it.
Temperature exponents and fit windows cause model-dependent shifts.
Zero-resistivity samples carry zero quoted error; they define transition intervals and are excluded from positive-branch least squares.

sequences.0.5: Below T=.45D unmeasured; activated positive resistivity from .45D to4D. No zero resistance observed.
sequences.0.3: Measured zero resistance .1-.325D; onset bracket(.325,.4]D; activated positive resistivity .4-4D.
sequences.0.2: Measured zero resistance .1-1.075D; onset bracket(1.075,1.15]D; positive resistivity with metallic T trend1.15-4D.

observable_statements.diffraction: One-site in-plane crystallographic period, equivalent transition-metal sites, and fourfold in-plane axis; no observed structural transition. Does not independently measure time reversal or every electronic order.
observable_statements.STS: Low-T spectra have a gap interval by the prompt, centered at plotted zero; only half-filled low-T chemical potential is explicitly fixed to that midpoint. Spatially uniform on the measured surface. Independent trace normalization and unknown matrix elements/background prevent an absolute spectral-weight sum-rule inversion. STS temperatures are only labeled low/high.
observable_statements.NMR: One line persists in each sample. Low-T relaxation is strongly suppressed. Empirical activation parameters characterize the measured rate; they are not automatically exact many-body singlet-triplet gaps. ν≈.2 has a suggestive coherence-like enhancement near the resistive onset, not a determination of pairing symmetry.
observable_statements.resistivity: Zero values define onset intervals, not exact transition temperatures or error-free finite weights in fits. Positive branches atν=.5,.3 show activated insulating trends;ν=.2 shows a metallic temperature trend. Zero resistance is consistent with superconductivity, but no Meissner or stiffness measurement was supplied.
observable_statements.inverse_problem: Local STS integrates over momentum with tunneling weights. Even if calibrated STS were the complete local spectral function, frequency Kramers–Kronig would yield only the local Green function; G(k,ω) and its momentum zero contour require a microscopic model or momentum-resolved information.

inverse_example.status: Mathematical/physical inverse-problem illustration only; not fit to any measurement and not proposed material Hamiltonian.
inverse_example.one_physical_orbital_Hamiltonian: H=Σ_kσ(ε_k−µ)n_kσ+U Σ_k n_k↑n_k↓. Interaction is local in momentum and infinite range in real space; all fermions are the physical one-orbital c.
inverse_example.state: T=0 spin-symmetric ensemble in singly occupied manifold: n_k↑=n_k↓=1/2, ν=1/2. Extensive spin degeneracy. NMR and transport have not been fitted; this is not proposed as a model of the samples.
inverse_example.momentum_relation: ε_minus(k)=ε_plus(k+Q), Q=(π,π). The local spectra are identical by relabeling momenta.
inverse_example.what_it_proves: A local spectral density and its frequency Kramers–Kronig transform do not identify the momentum assignment of G or the Γ-side zero area. This does not assert matching of NMR, transport, diffraction, or all other material constraints.
